# Psalm 138 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** By David. I will thank you, LORD, with everything I have! I will sing your praises in the presence of every other so-called god.

**2** I bow toward your holy temple and thank your name for your faithful love and reliability. You have honored your word above everything else.

**3** The day I called out, you answered me — you filled me with inner strength.

**4** Every king on earth will thank you, LORD, when they hear the promises you've spoken.

**5** They will sing about the LORD's ways, because the LORD's glory is immense.

**6** Even though the LORD is high above, he pays attention to the humble — but he sees through the proud from a distance.

**7** Even when I walk through the worst trouble, you keep me alive. You reach out against my enemies' fury, and your right hand rescues me.

**8** The LORD will finish what he started in my life. LORD, your faithful love lasts forever — don't abandon what your hands have made!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **138:6**: God pays close attention to the humble but only watches the proud from far away. Humility draws God near; pride keeps him at a distance. That's the divine operating system.

- **138:8**: 'The LORD will finish what he started in my life.' That's the promise: God doesn't start projects and abandon them. If he's working in you, he'll complete it.

— PNEUMA
